content:
A TODO item in Physlib currently looks like: 

TODO "63B7X" "Prove lemmas relating to the commutation rules of `dropPair` and `prodP`."

where here "63B7X" is a unique tag to uniquely identify the TODO item.

I don't think this is the best way of doing things, in particular, as it adds a burden on the user to add the unique tag. I think a much easier way would be to uniquely identify the TODO item by a hash of the comment. Not sure how easy this would be to implement though, and I suspect will have to rely on Leans FFI.

I also wonder here how easy the following would be:

The TODO items in Physlib are currently found here:

  • https://physlib.io/TODOList

It would be nice if we could get an AI to add the following info:

  • Additional context for the TODO item which may not be readable from the human-written script themselves.
  • A step-by-step plan to completing the TODO item.
  • Give them a score out of 100 of how easy it thinks they are.

I don't know the practicalities of doing something like this but I think it would likely make these TODO items a lot more useful.
FYI: The TODO list (nor the docs) are not currently up to date on the website, trying to get it fixed. But don't rely on this a definitive source for the time being.
I added a Github issue related to TODO items here: Physlib#1594.
